quote: I'd I'd like to see if I could schedule someone to come and meet me. It is about an hour a little over an hour away from me, and I don't drive.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly asked for an in-person visit and explained why (no driving, disability, dependence on family). The agent never revisited this — the call outcome is a phone appointment. This is a real unresolved mismatch between what was requested and what was booked, not a resolved substitution.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the agent may know phone-only is standard for this appointment type regardless of request, making the silent conversion procedurally normal rather than a miss. However nothing in the transcript confirms the agent registered or explained this to the customer, so the reactive read holds.
coaching_implication: Coach the agent to explicitly acknowledge and address format-change requests: 'I know you'd mentioned wanting someone in person — just so you know, this appointment will be over the phone, is that still okay?' Silent conversions risk a confused or frustrated customer at appointment time.

quote: Hi there, Ella. I am, someone who had already I set up the meeting, and I got really sick.

quote: Yeah. So I can just set up a phone call appointment for you. It looks like you're already assigned to a specialist.
stewart_read: The call closes with logistics confirmed (day, time, rep name, text follow-up promised) but no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, no one-hour block statement, and no no-driving/computer instruction — button-up mechanics are thin even though a date and time were locked.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: because this is a reschedule of an existing appointment rather than a first-time booking, some button-up elements (hour block, computer/no-driving framing) may have already been delivered in the original setter call and don't need repeating. But nothing in this transcript confirms that, so the safer read is that these elements were simply skipped.
coaching_implication: Even on reschedules, restate the appointment mechanics (duration, no-driving, sit-down-at-computer) briefly — the customer's transportation and health situation makes her a higher no-show risk, so the mechanics matter more here, not less.

quote: I didn't get a chance to meet him. Okay?
